target_customer: Law enforcement agencies investigating sex trafficking
problem: Traffickers advertise on classified sites where listings appear and vanish quickly. Rescue Forensics built search software to collect, track and document these ads as evidence.
business_model: Free for law enforcement at launch with premium features planned
product_category: Digital forensics for anti-trafficking investigations (Rescue Ops)

founders.name: Ryan Dalton
education: Law school (school not named in opened source)
founders.background_notes: Built a halfway house in Reynosa, Mexico at 18 and started an anti-trafficking department at Operation Broken Silence during law school, per TechCrunch.

founders.name: Brandon Hamric
founders.background_notes: Described as co-founder by TechCrunch and CTO by YC. No further background found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Scraping and archiving fast changing classified listings at scale, with search and tracking, is standard engineering with some hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Accumulated archive of listings has value, but the scraping approach is copyable and the product was free.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The big mobile forensics vendors in 2015 sold device extraction tools, a different job. The acquirer turned out to be IST Research, a defense and intelligence contractor.

market_need_then: TechCrunch reported several hundred state and local agencies in the US and Europe using the software and nine victims rescued, which shows real demand from investigators.

branding.domain_note: rescueforensics.com now redirects to a domain broker page, so the domain lapsed.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission driven anti-trafficking framing in launch press.

branding.community_and_virality: Launch coverage by TechCrunch in February 2015.

brand_strength.rationale: A clear mission story earned launch press, but no lasting brand assets or community found.

outcome_analysis: Rescue Forensics served law enforcement with a free tool for tracking trafficking related ads and reported traction with hundreds of agencies early on. Sources record an acquisition by IST Research, with the date conflicting between December 2016 and April 2019. YC marks the company inactive because of that exit, so the story is a small team absorbed into a contractor, with no public price or terms.
notes: The website redirected to a domain broker page (dead site). Acquisition rests on Mergr (Dec 2016) and CB Insights (April 2019 news item), so the date is left null. The 125K June 2015 round rests on a single aggregator (TheCompanyCheck, via search summary). CB Insights reports 720K over 3 rounds with Two Six Technologies and Innova Memphis as investors; recorded rounds total 205K so about 515K is unaccounted for and undated. TechCrunch reports 80K seed in February 2015 and names no competitors. Search found only 2015 device forensics vendors, which do the same category loosely, so the competitor list is empty. Founded year not found. Education for founders not found beyond law school.
